record.paper_title: Problem collection from the IML programme: Graphs, Hypergraphs, and Computing
record.context_brief: Algorithms for minimum k-arc-strong spanning subdigraphs
record.original_question: Is there a polynomial-time algorithm that, given a k-arc-strong tournament T=(V,A), finds a minimum-size arc set A0 of size β_k(T) whose induced spanning subdigraph is already k-arc-strong?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 11.4. [2] There exists a polynomial algorithm for finding, in a given k-arc-strong tournament T = (V, A) a minimum set of arcs A0 (of size βk(T)) such that the subdigraph induced by A0 is already k-arc-strong.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $T = (V, A)$ be a finite directed graph (digraph) without loops, where between any two distinct vertices $u, v \in V$ exactly one of the arcs $(u,v)$ or $(v,u)$ belongs to $A$ (i.e., $T$ is a tournament). For a positive integer $k$, the digraph $T$ is called $k$-arc-strong if $|V| \geq 2$ and for every set $F \subseteq A$ with $|F| < k$ the digraph $(V, A \setminus F)$ is strongly connected (every vertex is reachable from every other by a directed path).

For a $k$-arc-strong tournament $T$, define
$$\beta_k(T) = \min\{ |A_0| : A_0 \subseteq A \text{ and } (V, A_0) \text{ is } k\text{-arc-strong} \}.$$

Question: Does there exist an algorithm that, given as input a positive integer $k$ and a $k$-arc-strong tournament $T = (V, A)$, outputs an arc set $A_0 \subseteq A$ with $|A_0| = \beta_k(T)$ such that the spanning subdigraph $(V, A_0)$ is $k$-arc-strong, and runs in time bounded by a polynomial in $|V|$ (and $k$)?
artifact.status_search_result: Searches reveal active recent work by Bang-Jensen, Yeo, and collaborators on related problems (e.g., bounds on the minimum number of arcs in a $k$-arc-strong spanning subdigraph, making a tournament $k$-strong by adding arcs, and decomposition conjectures), and polynomial algorithms are known in restricted classes such as extended semicomplete and semicomplete bipartite digraphs. However, no source found explicitly asserts that the conjecture of a polynomial-time algorithm computing $\beta_k(T)$ for general $k$-arc-strong tournaments has been resolved; the status appears unsettled in the literature accessed.

status_evidence.title: Making a tournament k-strong
status_evidence.snippet: Every tournament on n ≥ k+1 vertices can be made k-strong by adding no more than (k+1 choose 2) arcs, resolving a 1994 conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Related additive problem about making tournaments k-strong has been resolved, but this is about adding arcs, not about polynomial-time minimization within an existing k-arc-strong tournament.

status_evidence.title: Spanning k-arc-strong subdigraphs with few arcs in k-arc-strong tournaments
status_evidence.snippet: Every strongly k-connected n-vertex semicomplete digraph contains a strongly k-connected spanning subgraph with at most kn + O(k^2) arcs.
status_evidence.claim: Existence/bound results known but do not establish a polynomial algorithm for computing the exact minimum β_k(T).

status_evidence.title: The Minimum Spanning Strong Subdigraph Problem for Extended Semicomplete and Semicomplete Bipartite Digraphs
status_evidence.snippet: Polynomial algorithms exist for the minimum spanning strong subdigraph in extended semicomplete and semicomplete bipartite digraphs; the general problem is NP-hard.
status_evidence.claim: Polynomial algorithms are known only in restricted classes; the general k-arc-strong tournament version remains a conjecture.
